description: Snowflake grammar constructs each previously rejected as an SQL syntax error: ALTER SESSION UNSET (single and comma-list), table aliases in UPDATE/DELETE (AS and bare), the NUMERIC(p,s) type and cast, PIVOT over a parenthesized subquery, CREATE TABLE ... LIKE (structure only, no data), keyword tokens as plain column names (CLUSTER/IDENTITY/CHANGES/STREAM/NETWORK/NUMERIC; START truly reserved - bare refused, quoted works; NEXT usable as column and alias), UNPIVOT as a CTE name, IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM null-safe comparison, reserved words as bare table aliases, START TRANSACTION ... COMMIT, PARTITION BY (a, b) parenthesized key lists, ALTER TABLE ADD without the COLUMN keyword (single and multi-column), keywords as VARIANT path keys (:, ., with casts, inside function arguments), and INSERT as the string function. Converted 1:1 from features/KeywordAndSyntaxCoverageTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ua (x INT, y INT)
UPDATE ua AS t SET t.x = 99 WHERE t.y = 20
SELECT x FROM ua WHERE y = 20
UPDATE ua u SET u.x = 5 WHERE u.y = 10
SELECT x FROM ua WHERE y = 10
DELETE FROM da AS d WHERE d.x = 2
CREATE TABLE pv (k INT, cat INT, v INT)
SELECT * FROM (SELECT cat, v FROM pv) PIVOT(SUM(v) FOR cat IN (10, 20)) p
CREATE TABLE src_like (a INT, b VARCHAR)
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE cp_like LIKE src_like
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'CP_LIKE'
CREATE TABLE rw (cluster INT, identity INT, changes INT, stream INT, network INT, numeric INT)
SELECT next + 1 AS next FROM nx
WITH unpivot AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT x FROM unpivot
SELECT 1 IS DISTINCT FROM 2, 1 IS DISTINCT FROM 1, NULL IS DISTINCT FROM 1, NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL, NULL IS DISTINCT FROM NULL
CREATE TABLE pw (a INT, b INT, x INT)
SELECT x FROM pw QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY (a, b) ORDER BY x) = 1 ORDER BY x
ALTER TABLE ac ADD checksum_group VARCHAR
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'AC'
SELECT v:database::VARCHAR AS a, v:update::VARCHAR AS b FROM vp
WITH r AS (SELECT {'create': 1, 'drop': 2, 'alter': {'show': 1}} AS j) SELECT j:create::int AS c, j:drop AS d, j:alter.show AS s1, j:alter:show AS s2 FROM r
SELECT v:from::VARCHAR, v:group::VARCHAR, v:order::VARCHAR, v:where::VARCHAR, v:case::VARCHAR FROM vp2
ALTER TABLE mc ADD b VARCHAR, c VARCHAR
